clips.caption:
He built the fifth-biggest online poker site in the world in ten months.

Then on Black Friday, the FBI seized his three biggest competitors' bank accounts. His own account was never touched — he'd done nothing wrong.

Most owners would have kept running quietly. Instead he shut the company down and personally paid back 41,000 players in four days, while his competitors took years, or never paid at all.

That collapse is what got him hired by casinos and Morgan Stanley. Kevin Trudeau's guest calls it the best thing that ever happened to his career.

What would you walk away from today if it meant building something bigger tomorrow?

#kevintrudeau #entrepreneur #businessstory #resilience #wealthmindset #successstory

A self-made investor turns down 99 out of every 100 pitches he hears.

Before he writes a check, he asks four questions: Is this person ride-or-die? Does anyone actually buy this product? Will it sell without you standing there explaining it? And can your team back up every claim you just made?

Kevin Trudeau's guest tells founders who claim a retail deal isn't signed yet: that's not a purchase order, that's a hope.

Most people pitch a dream. He's checking for proof.

Which of these four would your own idea actually pass right now?

#kevintrudeau #investing #entrepreneur #startuptips #businessadvice #wealthmindset

Your income is the average of your five closest friends. Kevin Trudeau's guest lived that math on purpose.

He skipped the friends who smoked weed and skateboarded and chose to hang around business people, athletes and celebrities instead — not for the status, but to study how they moved and thought.

The payoff showed up in conversation. Tell a friend "Costco owes me two million dollars" and they hear bragging. Tell a mentor the same thing and they hand you a banker's number to fix it.

Same sentence. Completely different world.

Are your five closest friends opening doors for you, or closing them?

#kevintrudeau #mindset #wealthmindset #successhabits #entrepreneur #richmindset

When COVID shut the world down, one franchise founder didn't slow down — he sped up.

While every other restaurant chain froze, he signed over 340 leases, locking in twelve months of free rent and huge improvement allowances landlords were desperate to give away. Kevin Trudeau's guest backed him early, and today that chain has grown to 98 locations.

It's the same move Aristotle Onassis made after World War II: everyone else saw a glut of ships nobody wanted. He saw a shortage coming and bought every ship he could, many of them for free.

Fear empties a market. That's exactly when the smart money moves in.

#kevintrudeau #entrepreneur #businessstory #wealthmindset #investing #opportunity

There's an old line that separates winners from everyone else: losers talk about people, winners talk about events.

Kevin Trudeau's guest says he'll cut off a phone call the second it turns into gossip about someone's coworker drama, even on a Sunday morning when he technically has the time.

His reasoning is blunt: his life is short, and there are only so many years to spend on payroll, marketing and growth, let alone somebody else's argument.

It's not that winners are above other people. They just have bigger fish to fry.

Where does your own conversation go when nobody's watching — people, or events?

#kevintrudeau #mindset #successhabits #entrepreneur #wealthmindset #productivity

If you want a certain kind of success, stop reading about it and go stand next to someone who already has it.

Kevin Trudeau's guest says his one piece of advice for anyone stuck is simple: go work for a winner in your exact category. Want to write bestsellers? Go be that author's assistant. Want to build a clothing empire? Go work for the guy who's already done four billion in sales.

Kevin backs it up with his own story — three days as a silent "fly on the wall" inside a billionaire's home, just watching how he ran his day.

Proximity teaches what books can't.

#kevintrudeau #mentorship #successhabits #entrepreneur #wealthmindset #careeradvice

The exact same business can be worth ten times more, depending on one decision.

Kevin Trudeau's guest breaks down the math: a company doing $5 million in sales might be worth $10 million privately — but the same business, taken public, can carry a $110 million valuation for no reason other than liquidity.

Put $1,000 into that private company and it grows to $10,000. Put it into the public version and that same growth is worth $100,000.

Nothing about the business changed. Only who could buy and sell it, and how fast.

Would you rather own 100% of something small, or a piece of something the whole market can trade?
